newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. CPI rose 0.3 pct in Oct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. CPI rose 0.3 pct in Oct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department said the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.3 percent in October, unchanged from the prior month. Excluding volatile food and energy items, the so-called "core" CPI was up 0.2 percent.
Experts had expected a 0.3-percent increase in the overall rate and a 0.2-percent rise in the core.
CHERYL KATZ, SENIOR ECONOMIST, MERRILL LYNCH & CO INC: "It was a little higher than we expected, (but) ... it tells you that inflation remains in check at the retail level."
ASTRID ADOLFSON, FIRST VICE PRESIDENT AND SENIOR ECONOMIST, MCM MONEYWATCH INC: "All the numbers were about in line with expectations.
"The inflation data were up in areas where it was expected and down in autos, where it was expected. (CPI was) so in line with consensus it couldn't be better.

As for the Treasury market's muted reaction, she added: "People really have to look at the underlying numbers, especially on consumption. Consumption could be a little bit different from what the overview might suggest."
October retail sales were released at the same time.
MARILYN SCHAJA, MONEY MARKET ECONOMIST, DONALDSON, LUFKIN & JENRETTE SECURITIES CORP: "The CPI number is right on expectations. It suggests the inflation picture is fine."

WILLIAM GRIGGS, MANAGING DIRECTOR, GRIGGS & SANTOW INC: "I don't know that it changes anything that we would've thought. We're still looking at an economy that doesn't seem to be plagued with a great deal of inflation."
